talks.summary:
### Offensive Evasion of Microsoft Advanced Threat Analytics
At 00:00, security researcher Siyu Zhu presents offensive research exploring evasion techniques against Microsoft Advanced Threat Analytics (ATA), an enterprise behavioral detection platform protecting Active Directory domain controllers.

### Microsoft ATA Sensor Architecture and Traffic Inspection
At 07:02, Zhu outlines ATA's deployment model. Operating via lightweight sensor agents installed on domain controllers, ATA inspects network traffic (Kerberos, DNS, RPC, NTLM) and Windows security event logs to detect adversarial reconnaissance and credential abuse.

### Circumventing Pass-the-Hash and Lateral Movement Detections
At 14:01, the speaker analyzes ATA's credential harvesting detections. He demonstrates how ATA detects suspicious NTLM authentication and Pass-the-Hash attacks from tools like Mimikatz, and details network timing tweaks that blend lateral movement into normal administrative traffic patterns.

### Evading Kerberos Golden Ticket and PAC Alerts
At 21:00, Zhu exposes bypasses targeting ATA's Kerberos anomaly heuristics. By matching encryption types (AES-128/256 rather than RC4), calibrating ticket expiration timestamps to match domain policy, and forging matching Privilege Attribute Certificates (PAC), attackers can generate Golden Tickets without triggering alerts.

### MS14-068 Privilege Escalation and Log Analysis Evasion
At 28:00, the presentation details weaponizing the MS14-068 Kerberos vulnerability while suppressing event log anomalies, demonstrating how attackers gain domain administrator privileges without alerting ATA sensors.

### Blue Team Detection Hardening
Concluding at 35:01, Zhu provides recommendations for enterprise defenders. He advises enabling Kerberos FAST armoring, auditing Event ID 4768 and 4769 ticket requests, and pairing network sensor analytics with dedicated host-level endpoint detection (EDR) on domain controllers.

talks.title: Killsuit How The Equation Group Remained Out Of Sight
talks.teaser: When the shadow brokers released a large number of Equation Group tools in 2017, many researchers jumped on the analysis of EternalBlue, FuzzBunch etc. The exploits of the leak have now been thoroughly analysed and mo...
talks.summary:
### Dissecting the Equation Group's Killsuit Framework
At 00:00, threat hunters Connor Morley and Lacie Fan present an in-depth reverse-engineering analysis of Killsuit, a highly sophisticated persistence and stealth framework attributed to the Equation Group, at the Blue Team Village.

### In-Memory Injection and Process Hijacking
At 04:57, the speakers examine Killsuit's execution flow. Tracing memory allocations, they illustrate how the framework injects malicious payloads into legitimate system processes without dropping executable binaries onto physical storage, evading conventional antivirus file scanners.

### Anti-Analysis Techniques and Encrypted Registry Storage
At 09:35, the presentation explores Killsuit's multi-layered defense mechanisms. The implant incorporates sophisticated anti-debugging checks and stores its modular component library encrypted directly within undocumented Windows registry keys, leaving static disk analysis ineffective.

### The pel_cheap Modular Loader Mechanism
At 14:02, Morley and Fan detail the internal mechanics of the `pel_cheap` loader. When an operational action is triggered, `pel_cheap` retrieves encrypted payload blobs from registry containers, decrypts them in volatile memory, and executes modular functionality entirely in RAM.

### Silent Error Suppression and Memory Hunting Strategies
Concluding between 19:58 and 25:58, the researchers reveal that Killsuit actively suppresses operating system error notifications to avoid alerting system administrators. They share actionable blue team hunting strategies, including YARA rules and memory scanning techniques to detect unbacked executable memory regions.

talks.title: When A Plan Comes Together Building a SOC A Team
talks.teaser: The security industry is facing a severe talent shortage, but the threats are growing in number and sophistication. Finding talent, honing it to meet your specific mission, and retaining it have become immense challen...
talks.summary:
### Building an Operational SOC "A-Team"
At 00:00, security operations veteran Mark Orlando presents a practical management and operational guide to designing, staffing, and modernizing enterprise Security Operations Centers (SOCs).

### Dismantling the Video Wall and Monitor Farm Myth
At 03:01, Orlando challenges the traditional image of the SOC as a tiered "monitor farm" where junior analysts sit in dark rooms staring at blinking SIEM dashboards. He argues that this visual spectacle model is structurally flawed, leading to severe alert fatigue and high staff attrition.

### Context-Driven Operations and Threat Prioritization
At 06:00, the speaker analyzes why SOCs fail to protect organizations. Operational alerts are frequently triaged in a vacuum without business context. High-performing security teams must understand core business assets, data flows, and regulatory exposures to prioritize incidents based on real organizational risk.

### Talent Retention, Career Pathways, and Burnout Mitigation
At 09:01, Orlando addresses the chronic turnover in security operations. Leaders must eliminate dead-end tier 1 roles by providing analysts with structured cross-training, dedicated time for proactive threat hunting, and clear career pathways into security engineering and incident response.

### Measuring Meaningful Operational Metrics
At 12:02, the presentation critiques traditional SOC performance metrics. Tracking raw numbers of closed tickets creates perverse incentives that encourage superficial reviews. Orlando advocates tracking operational outcome metrics, such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD), Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR), and dwell time reduction.

### Fostering a Blameless Culture of Continuous Improvement
Concluding at 15:00, Orlando outlines the core culture of a true SOC "A-Team." Successful security operations require blameless post-mortems, collaborative purple-teaming exercises with red teams, and empowering frontline analysts to author new detection logic and automated triage workflows.

talks.teaser: The life of a blue-teamer is daunting. There are logs to sift through, tasks to automate, incidents to triage, vulnerabilities to manage, meetings to attend, coffee to drink, etc. Scenarios have moving parts, procedur...
talks.summary:
### Navigating Early-Career Cybersecurity Operations
At 00:00, security engineer Christine Le shares practical advice and survival strategies for analysts entering defensive cybersecurity at the Blue Team Village. Le addresses the steep learning curve and operational challenges faced by newcomers in enterprise security.

### Overcoming Operational Overwhelm in the SOC
At 04:03, Le discusses managing the overwhelming volume of alerts and specialized tooling in modern Security Operations Centers (SOCs). She encourages junior analysts to focus on mastering foundational concepts rather than feeling pressured to understand every proprietary tool immediately.

### Cross-Functional Security Communication
At 08:15, the presentation highlights communication skills. Le explains that blue teamers must effectively translate complex cryptographic concepts and vulnerability assessments into actionable, non-adversarial business language when collaborating with external departments and software developers.

### Leveraging Automation and Scripting to Scale
At 12:22, the speaker urges analysts to automate routine tasks. By developing basic Python and Bash scripting skills, defenders can automate repetitive log analysis and endpoint triage, reducing operational fatigue while building valuable engineering competencies.

### Sustaining Growth and Intellectual Curiosity
Concluding between 16:30 and 21:33, Le emphasizes the importance of a growth mindset in a rapidly shifting industry. She provides guidance on avoiding burnout, building peer support networks, and actively engaging with the broader cybersecurity community to foster long-term career success.

talks.title: Serverless Log Analysis On AWS
talks.teaser: In this talk we will go over traditional log analysis methods for AWS Cloudtrail logs and why we needed to find a better way of performing such investigations. We will then dive into AWS Athena which is essentially a ...
talks.summary:
### Scalable Serverless Log Triage on AWS
At 00:00, Georgios Kapoglis (Incident Responder at Verizon Media) presents an architecture for serverless log aggregation and threat detection across enterprise AWS cloud environments.

### Ingestion of Multi-Account Cloud Telemetry
At 06:01, Kapoglis explains how centralized logging pipelines aggregate AWS CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and CloudWatch metrics from hundreds of AWS accounts into a centralized Amazon S3 security bucket.

### Cost-Effective Querying with Amazon Athena
At 12:01, the speaker details the economics of serverless threat hunting using Amazon Athena. Running Presto-based SQL queries directly against compressed S3 logs costs only $5 per terabyte scanned, eliminating the massive server maintenance overhead of traditional dedicated SIEM clusters.

### Templated SQL Threat Hunting Queries
At 18:00, the presentation showcases pre-authored SQL hunting queries. Frontline analysts can execute templated queries to detect IAM privilege escalation, abnormal cross-region API usage, and unauthorized modifications to S3 bucket access control policies.

### Columnar Optimization with Parquet and Glue
Concluding between 24:00 and 30:01, Kapoglis demonstrates performance tuning using AWS Glue ETL crawlers to convert raw JSON logs into columnar Apache Parquet format. This reduces data scan volumes by 80-90%, drastically cuts query latency, and feeds automated alerts into AWS Lambda for rapid incident containment.

talks.teaser: Memhunter is an endpoint sensor tool specialized in detecting memory-resident malware.  The detection process is performed through a combination of endpoint data collection and memory inspection scanners. Memhunter au...
talks.summary:
### Automated Detection of In-Memory Resident Threats
At 00:00, security researcher Carlos Garay introduces Memhunter, an open-source endpoint detection tool designed to identify and remediate fileless, memory-resident malware, at the Blue Team Village. Garay discusses the rise of memory-only attacks in modern adversary campaigns.

### The Mechanics of Fileless Malware Execution
At 08:33, Garay reviews how fileless malware evades disk-based endpoint protection. Adversaries leverage malicious macros, living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins), and Win32 memory APIs (such as `VirtualAllocEx` and `WriteProcessMemory`) to inject shellcode directly into trusted Windows processes.

### Endpoint Scanning Heuristics and Memory Inspection
At 16:43, the presentation explores Memhunter's scanning architecture. The tool analyzes running processes to detect unbacked executable pages, abnormal thread start addresses, and modified export tables, generating structured alerts without imposing heavy system overhead.

### Live Process Freezing and Forensic Analysis
At 25:13, Garay demonstrates Memhunter's active intervention capabilities. Upon detecting suspicious memory activity, the utility temporarily suspends the offending process threads, freezing malicious execution in place while performing deeper heuristic analysis.

### Detecting Process Hollowing and RWX Memory Pages
Concluding between 33:38 and 40:00, the speaker details techniques for identifying process hollowing and anomalous Read-Write-Execute (RWX) memory allocations. He outlines how blue teams can integrate Memhunter telemetry into SIEM pipelines to automate memory threat hunting across enterprise fleets.
